court-42.claim: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners. Delhi Police stopped their march to the Court on Bhagwant Das Road, and counsel filed the petition shortly before the filing counter closed. LiveLaw reported that the leaders then went to the Registry, and that a large crowd gathered inside the Court's precincts. The petition asks for the SIR to be suspended in every state while the case is heard, for a committee under a retired Supreme Court judge to audit the names left off or deleted, and for the Commission's files on its decision to hold the revision. PTI reported that the Registry flagged more than ten defects in it, among them illegible or missing pages, an unclear copy of Kharge's identity card and a court fee short by over Rs 200. LawBeat reported that the Registry registered it on 13 October once the defects were cured.
court-42.note: Second reading, 15 Oct 2026. court-43.claim: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition to the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, LiveLaw reported. Bar and Bench and LawBeat reported that the bench tagged it with the SIR cases already pending. The Chief Justice said the Court would ask one of the petitioners about his conduct at the next hearing, and that issuing notice did not mean the Court was condemning anything, Bar and Bench reported. He said notice on that petitioner's behalf would be entertained on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct. The bench did not name him. Notice was also issued on separate petitions by AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi and Congress leader Digvijaya Singh. No interim order and no date for the next hearing were reported.

court-44.headline: 'Nobody Can Browbeat Us' : Supreme Court In Plea Against October 12 March By Opposition Leaders; Issues Notice
court-44.claim: The same bench issued notice on a petition by four advocates about the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October, and on a second plea seeking similar relief, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for rules on demonstrations near the Supreme Court and the High Courts and for criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and Mahua Moitra. Senior counsel for the petitioners said about 200 lawyers had signed a memorandum calling the march browbeating. The Chief Justice said nobody could browbeat the Court and that the judges knew what was said outside it. The Court directed all law enforcement agencies to preserve the CCTV footage and other digital material they had collected, and LiveLaw reported that it also directed footage of the Court's premises to be preserved. Bar and Bench reported that notice went to the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, and that the Court declined to begin contempt proceedings that day.
court-44.note: Second reading, 15 Oct 2026. LiveLaw 554802 opened (15 Oct, 1:13 pm IST): W.P.(C) No. 1360/2026, Diary No. 64394/2026, four advocate petitioners, contempt against the four named leaders, 200 lawyers' memorandum, and the quote all verbatim ('"Nobody can browbeat us," the CJI responded.' and '"We are not sitting in ivory towers. We know what statements they make outside and what they say in Court. We know everything," the CJI said.'). The page's visible headline and title say 'By Opposition Leaders'; only its og:title says 'By Political Leaders', so the headline is corrected to the visible one. LiveLaw also says notice issued 'on two pleas seeking similar reliefs'; added. Bar and Bench's live updates (item 30) record the dictated order as 'all law enforcement agencies are directed to preserve the CCTV footage or any other digital material collected by them', 'as agreed to among the parties'; the preservation of the Court's own footage is LiveLaw's summary line only, so it is now attributed. Bar and Bench (live, and report 'Supreme Court issues notice to Congress, Rahul Gandhi on plea against march to Court, X post against CJI') gives the CJI's words as 'Nobody can browbeat the judiciary' where LiveLaw has 'Nobody can browbeat us'; the claim paraphrases and the quote follows LiveLaw, the cited outlet. That report also says notice went to the Congress, Gandhi and other leaders, that respondents include the Union, the Congress, Gandhi, Kharge, the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, Moitra and Akhilesh Yadav, and that the contempt prayer concerns a post by the Kerala Congress's X account addressed to the CJI; LiveLaw puts the contempt prayer against the four leaders. Not resolved; the claim keeps LiveLaw's four and does not quote the post. 'No contempt today. We are only issuing notice.' confirmed in both Bar and Bench pieces. The four advocates are named by Bar and Bench and LiveLaw and are not named here; senior counsel is named by role. No next date reported.

court-45.claim: The Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors whose names were left off Delhi's roll after they moved house and could not fill the enumeration form. They had asked the Court to quash para 4(c) of the SIR guidelines and to change the procedure that requires such electors to seek fresh inclusion through Form 6, and to restore their entries and let them move them to their new address through Form 8. The Commission's standing counsel said they could file Form 6 and that the Electoral Registration Officer would help. The first petitioner said that filing Form 6 would be a false declaration. The bench said that, since the suggestion came from the Commission's counsel on the officer's instructions, his fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced. It closed the petition and said the petitioners could file Form 6 if they wished, to be processed in accordance with law. It did not decide the challenge to the guidelines.
court-45.note: Second reading, 19 Oct 2026. The order PDF LiveLaw links (https://www.livelaw.in/pdf_upload/2026/10/16/3-706943.pdf) downloaded again with curl and read in full: SHA-256 a2eb7da066bbac363a8c3ddc6f055990ca40d923003f8a99febd50187cd3147f, the same file the first reader read. W.P.(C) 14955/2026 with CM APPL. 70130/2026 and 70131/2026, CNR DLHC010486872026, order of 14.10.2026, Justice Dinesh Mehta and Dr. Justice Aditi Choudhary, 'downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/10/2026 at 22:07:13'. The quote (paras 6 and 7, with '...' over the para number) is verbatim, curly apostrophe in 'no.1’s' included. Paras 3 and 4 support the response: counsel said the grievance 'can be redressed if they choose to fill/furnish Form 6 prescribed under Rule 25(2) read with Rule 13(1)(a)', and that at the previous hearing he had asked petitioner no.1 to fill it and assured that the Electoral Registration Officer would assist. Para 5: the first petitioner, in person, 'submitted that if they furnish a Form 6, it would be a false declaration'. One correction: the claim said para 4(c) 'sends such electors to Form 6 with the declaration'. Neither the order nor LiveLaw says what 4(c) provides or mentions any declaration in it; the prayers ask to quash 4(c) (prayer A) and to recast the procedure 'instead of requiring them to seek fresh inclusion through Form 6' (prayer B). The claim now says that, and adds that the petition was closed without deciding the challenge, which is what para 7 does. The order does not mention item (iii), 'first time', or section 31. Para 2 says the names 'got deleted from the electoral' (sic); on the site's terms they were left off, as the petition's own words ('could not be enumerated during the SIR') show. LiveLaw 555029 opened (Nupur Thapliyal, datePublished 2026-10-16T14:49:29+05:30, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1014): its text agrees and adds nothing beyond the order. The petitioners are private persons and are not named. Tags (Form 6, Documents and declaration, Form 8; Delhi High Court) fit.
